notes: wowsims-forever models one Hunter spell package for all three specs; Survival keeps the same Aimed Shot / Multi-Shot base as the other two, and, unlike Beast Mastery or Marksmanship, weaves in melee Raptor Strike -- the Survival tree's talents (Counterattack, Improved Wing Clip and the rest) are the ones that make standing in melee worthwhile. The cited Warcraft Tavern guide says outright that you should never prioritize Serpent Sting over an Aimed Shot or Multi-Shot cast; Serpent Sting is therefore ordered below both shots here, refreshed only once it is about to fall off and neither shot is close to ready, the same shape as hunter-marksmanship's. Raptor Strike is on-next-swing: its APL-castable queue is tag 3 (pipeline/apl.py's ON_NEXT_SWING_QUEUE_TAG, the odd one out among the on-next-swing abilities, which otherwise queue at tag 1), not the tag 1 that Heroic Strike, Cleave and Maul use, so it is cast with tag 3 here. It is gated on mana so it does not pull mana away from the ranged shots below 20 percent. Every rank named here is checked against this build's own spellconst: the shared preset names Multi-Shot as spell 25294, which does not exist in this build (Multi-Shot only has one rank here, 2643), and calls Serpent Sting rank 8 when 25295 is actually rank 9 -- both fixed here rather than copied stale. Fix round 3: the whole body of sim/hunter/aimed_shot.go's registerAimedShotSpell is commented out, so 20904 is never registered by any hunter build in this engine; the cast line is kept (this is the guide's actual rotation and the engine follow-up is to register it) and declared inert rather than deleted. Aimed Shot being unregistered also makes every spellTimeToReady(20904) reference in this file resolve to a nil APLValue, which an `and` condition silently drops (rot.newValueAnd filters nil operands) rather than nulling the whole condition -- so Serpent Sting's gate above already degrades correctly to its other operand and did not need rewriting. What did need fixing: nothing in this site's request pipeline (sim/request) ever sets a character's DistanceFromTarget, so every hunter starts at 0 -- under Multi-Shot, Serpent Sting and Aimed Shot's own ExtraCastCondition floor of 12 (core.MinRangedAttackDistance), which also gates the ranged auto-attack itself (sim/core/attack.go's startPull). A `move` prepull action to 30 yards is added so this and every future simulation of this spec actually has a ranged auto-attack and can cast its ranged abilities -- matching the priority order above, which already ranks Aimed Shot ahead of Raptor Strike. That has a real cost specific to this spec: Raptor Strike's own ExtraCastCondition requires DistanceFromTarget <= 5 (core.MaxMeleeAttackDistance), a genuine dead zone against the ranged floor of 12 in this engine's distance model, so once the character commits to 30 yards for the ranged kit it can never re-enter melee range on a stationary single-target fight and Raptor Strike's line goes unreached; this is an existing limitation of a single static `move`, not a new regression (Raptor Strike was not firing before this fix either), and is left as a follow-up rather than solved here with a dynamic kite-and-swap the APL value language does not have a clean way to express (the same category of gap mage-frost's own notes call out for powershifting). Under this smoke build specifically (no gear equipped anywhere) the ranged weapon's SwingSpeed is the Weapon{} zero value, which collapses the ranged swing timer to its 500ms cast-time floor (sim/core/attack.go's WeaponAttack.updateSwingDuration: curSwingDuration = weapon.SwingSpeed / hasteMultiplier = 0) -- a real ranged weapon's positive SwingSpeed does not have this problem. The resulting sub-GCD auto-shot loop saturates the character's action economy so completely that the priority list, including Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting, never gets a decision window in this one bare-weapon run; this is a new engine-side artifact of the no-gear smoke build (recorded for the engine ledger), not a defect in this rotation's gates.

Raptor Strike as the melee filler while Survival's talents make meleeing worthwhile; queued at tag 3, the engine's odd one out for on-next-swing abilities. Never below 20 percent mana, so it does not starve the ranged shots.

Serpent Sting kept up whenever it is about to fall off -- never ahead of Aimed Shot or Multi-Shot above, per the cited guide.
